cohort: 215 women with insulin-treated Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), non-anomalous singleton pregnancy who delivered at a single tertiary center between March 2012 and May 2018
finding: Although over 40% of newborns delivered by women with insulin-dependent T2DM experienced hypoglycemia, there was no significant difference in the risk based on the mode of delivery or the use of intrapartum insulin infusion.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the risk of neonatal hypoglycemia between newborns delivered vaginally versus by planned cesarean delivery.
